gaps.sentence: Barely ___ the ink dried when the complaints began to arrive.
gaps.explanation: 'Barely had the ink dried when …' — inverted past perfect.

gaps.sentence: ___ the storm passed did the ferries resume service.
gaps.explanation: Only after/once the storm passed did… — fronted 'only' phrase.

gaps.sentence: Not only ___ the play cancelled, but the theatre was closed as well.
gaps.explanation: 'Not only was the play cancelled' — inverted passive.

gaps.sentence: Come ___ it may, the trial must proceed.
gaps.explanation: 'Come what may' — fixed inverted idiom = whatever happens.

gaps.sentence: So loud ___ the music that the neighbours called the police.
gaps.explanation: 'So loud was the music that …' — fronted 'so + adj' with inversion.

gaps.sentence: Only after the audit ___ the missing funds come to light.
gaps.explanation: 'Only after the audit did the funds come to light'.

gaps.sentence: Scarcely had the plane taken ___ when the alarm sounded.
gaps.explanation: 'Taken off' completes the phrasal verb inside the inverted 'scarcely had … when' structure.

gaps.sentence: Under no circumstances ___ the door be left unlocked.
gaps.explanation: 'Under no circumstances should/must the door be left unlocked' — modal + inversion.
